# Vidhu Sarwal — Portfolio Site Specification

**Status:** Build spec for Claude Code
**Owner:** Vidhu Sarwal
**Reference aesthetic:** [vicharak.in](https://vicharak.in) — clean, technical, premium, restrained
**Goal:** A portfolio that reads as built by a designer with taste, not generated by an AI template.

---

## 0. Design Philosophy (read this first)

This is **not** a generic developer portfolio. It is a single-narrative scroll experience that uses a 3D single-board computer as the storytelling vehicle for the candidate's body of work. Every animation must feel **inevitable, not decorative**. If an effect could be removed without weakening the narrative, remove it.

**Three rules that override anything else in this doc:**

1. **Restraint over abundance.** Half the polish comes from what is *not* on screen. Whitespace is a feature.
2. **Motion serves story.** No animation exists for its own sake. Every transition either reveals new content, anchors orientation, or rewards attention.
3. **Black is the canvas.** Color is used like ink on paper — sparingly, where it must direct the eye. No gradient backgrounds. No accent rainbows. No glassmorphism.

**The taste benchmark:** if a visitor screenshots any single frame, it should look intentional. Frames mid-transition should not look like glitches.

---

## 0.5 Design Direction Note

The SBC is the centerpiece of the site but it is **a static beautiful object, not a tour**. The camera does not fly around it. The board sits in a fixed pose with slow continuous rotation (like a museum pedestal) and projects appear as typographic cards beside it. As the user scrolls past each card, the SBC's lighting subtly shifts — a soft accent rim light moves to the relevant board feature — but the board itself stays anchored.

This is a deliberate restraint choice. Scroll-locked camera choreography around 3D objects was the breakout portfolio pattern of 2023–2024 and is now saturated. The Vicharak reference aesthetic — the benchmark for this build — is **not heavy on scroll choreography**; it is heavy on typography, restraint, and architectural layout. The most prestigious portfolios in 2026 trend toward less animation, not more.

The signature "wow" moment is concentrated in the §5 transition where the grid dissolves and the SBC arrives. After that, the site quiets down and lets the content breathe.

---

## 1. Visual Identity

### 1.1 Color System

```
--bg-base:        #080808   /* jet black, never pure #000 (reads flat on OLED) */
--bg-elevated:    #0E0E0E   /* cards, slight elevation */
--border-rest:    rgba(255,255,255,0.06)   /* invisible until hovered */
--border-active:  rgba(255,255,255,0.45)   /* glow target */
--text-primary:   #F4F4F2   /* off-white, less harsh than #FFF */
--text-secondary: #8A8A88   /* metadata, captions */
--text-tertiary:  #4A4A48   /* deep mute */
--accent:         #C8E4FF   /* desaturated ice blue — USED SPARINGLY */
```

**Accent usage policy:** the ice blue appears in ≤ 3 places site-wide:
- The dot at the end of the scroll spline
- Hover state on actionable links (project titles, contact)
- Currently-active section label in nav

That's it. If you find yourself reaching for it elsewhere, use `--text-primary` or `--text-secondary` instead.

### 1.2 Typography

- **Display / headings:** [Cabinet Grotesk](https://fontshare.com/fonts/cabinet-grotesk) (medium 500, bold 700). Confident, slightly editorial, not generic geometric sans.
- **Body / paragraphs:** [Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/) (regular 400, medium 500). The boring correct choice.
- **Mono / code / labels:** [JetBrains Mono](https://www.jetbrains.com/lp/mono/) (regular 400). Used for section indices ("01 / HERO"), project metadata, and small caps labels.

**Scale (clamp for fluid):**
```
H1 hero:   clamp(56px, 9vw, 144px)   /* tight leading: 0.95 */
H2 section: clamp(40px, 5vw, 72px)
H3 project: clamp(24px, 2.5vw, 36px)
Body:       clamp(15px, 1vw, 17px)   /* leading 1.6 */
Mono label: 11px uppercase, letter-spacing 0.15em
```

### 1.3 Spacing & Grid

12-column grid, 24px gutter, max content width 1440px with 80px side margins on desktop. Sections are separated by `clamp(160px, 20vh, 240px)` of vertical breathing room — generous, not cramped.

---

## 2. Tech Stack

```
Framework:       Next.js 15 (App Router, RSC where it helps, client where needed)
Language:        TypeScript (strict mode)
Styling:         Tailwind CSS v4 + CSS custom properties for runtime values
3D:              Three.js + @react-three/fiber + @react-three/drei
Animation:       GSAP 3 + ScrollTrigger + DrawSVG (Club GSAP — free for personal)
Smooth scroll:   Lenis (@studio-freight/lenis)
3D model format: .glb (compressed with Draco)
Deployment:      Vercel
```

**The entire stack is JavaScript/TypeScript on Node.** No Rust, no WASM, no Go. Standard Vercel deployment target. The only build step beyond `next build` is asset optimization (Draco compression on the .glb, which is a one-time CLI command at build time).

**Why this stack:**
- Next.js for routing, image optimization, deploy ergonomics. No need for SSR-as-feature here; this is a single-page narrative.
- React Three Fiber because it makes Three.js declarative and lets the 3D scene be controlled by the same React state that controls the HTML overlays.
- GSAP over Framer Motion because **scroll-synchronized, timeline-based, SVG-aware** animation is GSAP's home turf. Framer Motion is fine for component transitions but fights you on scrubbed scroll timelines.
- Lenis is non-optional. Native scroll on Chrome/Safari/Firefox feels different on every OS. Lenis normalizes it.

**Do NOT add:** Framer Motion (collision with GSAP), Locomotive Scroll (Lenis is the modern choice), Spline (the design tool — too heavy, replace with R3F), any UI component library (everything is custom).

## 2.5 Configuration & Environment

The site has a small number of toggles controlled via environment variables. These are read at build time. Vercel project settings expose them in the dashboard.

**File: `.env.local`** (gitignored, local dev) and Vercel env settings (production):

```bash
# Project visibility toggles
NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_SAMSUNG=true     # set to "false" to hide Samsung PRISM project everywhere
NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_LKMP=true        # set to "false" to hide Linux Kernel Mentorship Program
NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_GSOC=true        # always true normally, kept for symmetry

# Contact endpoint (if a form is ever added)
NEXT_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL=vidhu.sarwal19@gmail.com

# Optional: analytics
NEXT_PUBLIC_VERCEL_ANALYTICS_ID=
```

**Behavior when `NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_SAMSUNG=false`:**
- The Samsung PRISM camera stop in §6 is **removed entirely** from the SBC scroll sequence
- The scroll narrative recalculates: 4 stops instead of 5, scroll distance shortens proportionally
- The Samsung card in the experience timeline (§7) is removed
- All Samsung-related tech connections in the constellation (§8) — anything tagged `samsung-only` — collapse silently
- No "this section is hidden" placeholder. The site behaves as if Samsung never existed in this version.

This lets you ship two builds from the same codebase: a public version and a version you send to specific recipients (e.g., when Samsung work is under post-internship discretion). Toggle in Vercel dashboard, redeploy, done.

**Implementation note:** read these flags into a typed `siteConfig` object at module load. Do not scatter `process.env` reads throughout the codebase.

```typescript
// lib/config.ts (illustrative — not the implementation)
export const siteConfig = {
  showSamsung: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_SAMSUNG !== 'false',
  showLKMP: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_LKMP !== 'false',
  showGSOC: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_GSOC !== 'false',
};
```

**Project list filtering must be data-driven.** Define the project array once with metadata flags; the renderer iterates and skips entries where the corresponding config flag is false. Do not hard-code conditional JSX per project.

## 3. Site Architecture

Single page, six scroll-locked sections:

```
01 / HERO           — Name, role, mouse-reactive grid wall
02 / TRANSITION     — Grand reveal: grid dissolves, SBC enters
03 / SBC SHOWCASE   — Projects shown beside the SBC; rim light moves between board features as you scroll
04 / EXPERIENCE     — Work history (Samsung, GSoC, LKMP) as horizontal timeline
05 / STACK          — Tech constellation
06 / CONTACT        — Closing, minimal
```

**Persistent UI elements (overlay layer, fixed position):**
- Top-left: monogram `VS.` or `V/S` (links to top)
- Top-right: section indicator (e.g., `02 / 06`)
- Right edge, vertically centered: **scroll spline** (see §6)
- Bottom-left on hero only: scroll hint that fades after first interaction

---

## 4. Section 01 — HERO

### 4.1 Layout

Full viewport. Content centered-left at roughly 8% from left edge, vertically centered.

```
[mono label]  01 / SYSTEMS ENGINEER
[H1]          Vidhu Sarwal.
[H2 muted]    Linux kernel · Distributed systems · AI infrastructure.
[separator]   thin 1px line, 80px wide, --border-active
[body]        Final-year CS undergrad. GSoC '25 at BeagleBoard.org.
              Samsung PRISM. Linux Kernel Mentorship Program.
[CTA row]     [View Work →]   [Get in touch]
```

The name uses a SplitText reveal on load: each character drops in from `y: 40px, opacity: 0` with a 0.04s stagger. Total animation < 700ms. No bounce easing — use `power3.out`.

### 4.2 The Grid Wall (background)

**This is the hero's signature element. It must be perfect.**

A canvas-rendered grid of small rounded squares filling the viewport behind the content. At rest, the grid is barely visible — borders at 6% white opacity. As the mouse moves, cells within a radius of the cursor brighten based on distance.

**Specs:**
- Cell size: 28px × 28px on desktop, 20px × 20px on mobile
- Gap between cells: 6px
- Cell corner radius: 6px
- Cell stroke width: 1px
- Light falloff radius: 180px from cursor center
- Falloff curve: smooth cubic, not linear (linear looks like a hard spotlight)
- Peak brightness at cursor: border opacity 0.55, with a subtle inner fill of `rgba(255,255,255,0.03)`
- Animation: lerp the brightness toward the target each frame, with `lerp factor 0.15` — gives the light a slight inertia, like real bloom

**Implementation must be Canvas 2D**, not DOM. With ~28px cells on a 1440×900 viewport you'd have ~1500 cells — DOM divs reacting to mousemove would stutter. Canvas redraws only the cells within the falloff radius each frame.

**Edge cases:**
- On window resize, recompute grid dimensions, don't just scale
- On `prefers-reduced-motion`, render the grid statically with no mouse reaction
- On touch devices, the grid is static (no fake cursor following)
- The grid must not block clicks on hero content — Canvas with `pointer-events: none`

### 4.3 Hero Exit Animation

When the user starts scrolling, the hero doesn't just slide up. The grid wall **disassembles**:
- Cells nearest the cursor "lift" (translate-Z forward, fade out) first
- Cells radiating outward follow with stagger based on distance from cursor at scroll-start moment
- Total dissolve: 800ms, locked to first 30% of the transition scroll distance
- Simultaneously, hero text fades and translates up subtly (-30px, opacity 1→0)

This is the handoff to Section 02.

---

## 5. Section 02 — TRANSITION (Grid → SBC)

This is a **pinned scroll section** lasting ~150vh of scroll distance. The viewport stays fixed; the animation scrubs with scroll.

**Choreography (0% → 100% of pinned scroll):**

| Progress | Event |
|----------|-------|
| 0–15%    | Grid disassembles (see §4.3) |
| 10–35%   | Camera starts in deep black; faint particles drift (depth cues) |
| 25–50%   | The stylized SBC fades in from black, far away, slowly rotating |
| 40–70%   | Camera dollies in toward the SBC; SBC rotates to a 3/4 hero angle |
| 60–90%   | A thin label types out: `S Y S T E M S · 2 0 2 3 — 2 0 2 6` |
| 85–100%  | Camera settles. SBC is now centered, lit, ready for Section 03 |

The SBC arrival is the "grande" moment. It must feel inevitable, like the grid was always there to dissolve into this.

**Lighting design for the SBC:**
- One key light, soft, top-front-left, color `#F4F4F2`
- One rim light, hard, behind-right, very low intensity, color `#C8E4FF` (the accent) — picks out the board edge
- Black environment HDRI (or a custom one with only subtle gradient — the board should not pick up environmental color)
- Slight bloom post-processing (`@react-three/postprocessing`, intensity 0.3 max — restraint)
- Faint contact shadow under the board, not a hard drop shadow

**Camera defaults:**
- FOV 35° (longer lens = more flattering, less distorted)
- Position starts at `(0, 0, 12)`, settles at `(0.5, 0.3, 4.5)` for hero pose

## 6. Section 03 — SBC SHOWCASE (Projects)

The SBC arrives at the end of §5 and stays on screen for this entire section. **The camera does not move.** The board sits in a fixed pose with slow continuous rotation (one full rotation every 60 seconds — barely perceptible motion that keeps the scene alive). As the user scrolls, project cards appear beside the board, and the lighting on the board shifts to highlight whichever board feature corresponds to the current project.

The metaphor: the board is the candidate's career. Each chip/connector is a chapter. The light moves through it. The board itself is constant.

### 6.1 Scene Layout

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                          │
│                                                          │
│   ┌─────────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────┐  │
│   │                     │         │ 03 / PROJECT 02  │  │
│   │     [SBC scene]     │         │                  │  │
│   │   slow rotation     │         │  Multimodal RAG  │  │
│   │   rim light moves   │         │  Platform        │  │
│   │                     │         │                  │  │
│   └─────────────────────┘         │  Samsung PRISM   │  │
│                                    │  body text...    │  │
│                                    └──────────────────┘  │
│                                                          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        Left 55% of viewport            Right 40% of viewport
```

- **Left column (55% width):** The SBC scene, pinned via ScrollTrigger for the duration of this section.
- **Right column (40% width):** Project cards scroll vertically through this column. Only one card is fully visible at a time.
- Total scroll distance for the section: ~250vh.

### 6.2 The SBC's Behavior

- **Pose:** 3/4 hero angle established at end of §5, no further camera moves.
- **Rotation:** continuous slow Y-axis rotation, ~6° per second, eased to a near-imperceptible breathing rhythm. Pauses subtly when the user is reading (paused if no scroll input for 3 seconds, resumes on scroll).
- **Lighting:** the key light stays fixed. **A second accent rim light moves** between board features based on scroll progress. Movement is interpolated smoothly along an invisible arc that traces above the board, not teleported between positions.
- **Heat-shimmer particles** appear briefly (1–2 seconds) on the SoC when the Samsung card enters the viewport. They fade as the scroll moves past. Subtle — a dozen particles, not a snowstorm.

### 6.3 The Five Projects (cards in order)

Each project is a card in the right column. When the card is closer to the vertical center of the viewport, its corresponding board feature is illuminated.

| Order | Project | Highlighted feature on board |
|-------|---------|------------------------------|
| 1 | **GSoC '25 — Embedded Linux / Mainline Patches** | Expansion connector (top-right block) |
| 2 | **Samsung PRISM — Multimodal RAG Platform** | Central SoC (with brief heat-shimmer) |
| 3 | **VaultCrypt — Distributed Storage in Go** | The two memory chips flanking the SoC |
| 4 | **GitScope — Codebase Intelligence** | Pin header along the long edge |
| 5 | **SIH 2024 + ESP32 IoT Relay** | Whole board, slight outward float, faint companion module visible briefly |

**Note on the Samsung entry:** when `NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_SAMSUNG=false`, this card is removed from the project list. The remaining 4 projects redistribute the scroll distance evenly. The SoC lighting state is skipped (the rim light passes from expansion connector → memory chips directly).

### 6.4 The Generic SBC Model (design spec)

This is a **stylized, minimalist mockup** of a single-board computer — not a reproduction of any specific board. The goal is silhouette clarity, not technical accuracy. A viewer who has never seen a real SBC should still read it as "a circuit board."

**Required components on the model (and nothing more):**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ▢ ▢ ▢ ▢ ▢ ▢ ▢ ▢ ▢ ▢ ▢ ▢ ▢ ▢  ← pin header (single row)
│                                              
│   ┌──────┐         ┌──────────┐    ┌───┐    
│   │ MEM  │         │          │    │   │ ← expansion header
│   └──────┘         │   SoC    │    │   │   (small block,
│                    │  (main)  │    └───┘    top-right)
│   ┌──────┐         │          │              
│   │ MEM  │         └──────────┘    ┌─┐ ┌─┐ ← two small connectors
│   └──────┘                         └─┘ └─┘   (USB-C style)
│                                              
│              ○                ○             ← mounting holes (4 corners)
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   ○                                      ○
```

**Specifications:**
- **Board:** rounded-rectangle PCB, dimensions ~85mm × 56mm proportion (credit-card-ish), corner radius 3mm, thickness 1.5mm. Surface color: deep matte charcoal (`#181818`), very slightly desaturated — not pure black, so it reads as separate from the background.
- **Main SoC:** centered, square chip ~18mm × 18mm, height 1.2mm. Color: matte black with a subtle bevel and a faint engraved square outline on top (suggests a die without specifying a brand). No logos, no text.
- **Memory chips:** two rectangular packages flanking the SoC, ~10mm × 6mm. Same matte black treatment.
- **Pin header:** a single row of ~20 pins along one long edge. Pins are tiny gold-tinted cylinders (use `#9C7B3C` muted, not bright gold). This is the only warm color on the model. Restrain it.
- **Expansion connector (top-right):** a small rectangular block ~12mm × 8mm, slightly raised. Reads as "where a daughterboard would plug in."
- **Two small connectors (right edge):** USB-C-style trapezoids, just enough to suggest I/O.
- **Mounting holes:** four small circles at the corners, slight inset shadow.
- **PCB surface detail:** very subtle trace lines (1px wide, slightly lighter than the board color, ~`#222`) that hint at routing without being legible as real circuits.

**Named meshes (required for runtime targeting):**
```
pcb                    → the board itself
soc                    → main central chip
mem_left, mem_right    → memory chips
pin_header             → the row of pins
expansion_connector    → top-right block
io_left, io_right      → USB-C-style trapezoids
```

The rim light targets these named meshes by querying the scene graph. If meshes are not named correctly, the lighting transitions cannot resolve.

**What the model does NOT have:**
- No brand logos, model numbers, silkscreen text, QR codes
- No RJ45/Ethernet jack, HDMI, audio jacks (too specific, too cluttered)
- No heatsink (would block the SoC anchor)
- No visible capacitors or small SMD components (clutter)
- No coin-cell battery, no antenna

**Modeling approach:** ~1 hour of work in Blender for someone who knows the tool. All primitives: rounded cubes, beveled edges, simple materials. Total polygon count target: < 20k triangles. No textures needed beyond the subtle trace pattern, which can be a single 1K normal map or a procedural shader.

**Material treatment in Three.js:**
- PCB: `meshStandardMaterial`, roughness 0.7, metalness 0.0
- Chips: `meshStandardMaterial`, roughness 0.4, metalness 0.1 (slight sheen)
- Pin header pins: `meshStandardMaterial`, roughness 0.3, metalness 0.8 (the metallic accent)
- Connectors: same as chips

The result should look like a high-end product render of a fictional board — the kind of mockup that might appear in a CPU vendor's keynote slide. Restrained, monochromatic, premium.

### 6.5 Project Card Structure

```
[mono index]      02 / PROJECT
[mono category]   AI INFRASTRUCTURE · 2025
[H3 title]        Multimodal Enterprise Knowledge Synthesis
[body 2-3 lines]  Async Python platform handling 61k LOC. LangGraph multi-agent
                  orchestration, hybrid retrieval (ChromaDB + BM25), Qwen-VL
                  document parsing. Adopted by multiple Samsung teams.
[meta row]        [Python] [LangGraph] [ChromaDB] [Qwen-VL]    [↗ Case study]
```

**Card animation:**
- Card enters from below with `y: 40px → 0`, `opacity: 0 → 1`, 600ms, `power2.out` easing
- Card exits upward with `y: 0 → -40px`, `opacity: 1 → 0`, faster (400ms) — leaving is quicker than arriving
- Cards are absolutely positioned; only one fully opaque at a time
- The `[↗ Case study]` link is a real anchor to a future project detail page (out of scope for v1 — render as styled but not yet linked)

### 6.6 The Perimeter Trace (signature detail)

A single thin glowing line traces around the perimeter of the PCB, drawn in 3D space using drei's `<Line>` component. The line's draw progress is tied to scroll position through the SBC section.

- At scroll-start of §6: 0% drawn
- At scroll-end of §6: 100% drawn (the line has traced the full perimeter)
- Color: `--accent` (ice blue), low opacity (~0.4), with a faint additive bloom
- Stroke width: 1.5px equivalent in 3D space
- The line appears to "flow" along the trace — a small bright dot leads the draw

This is the visual metaphor: scrolling traces the signal path. It is also the **only animated 3D element in §6 beyond the slow rotation and rim-light movement**. Keep it that way. No additional glowing things on the board.

### 6.7 Performance Constraints

- Total scene polygon count: ≤ 80k triangles (much lower than a multi-stop version would need)
- Textures: 1K max, compressed (KTX2 / Basis)
- Use Draco compression on the .glb
- Lazy-load the SBC model on entering §5; show a thin progress indicator (1px line growing across the screen)
- `<Canvas frameloop="demand">` and `invalidate()` only when rim light needs to interpolate or scroll changes
- On mobile, the right-column cards stack below the SBC instead of beside it; rotation continues but post-processing bloom is disabled
- The perimeter trace simplifies to a single static glowing outline on mobile (no progressive draw)

## 7. Section 04 — EXPERIENCE TIMELINE

After the SBC narrative, transition to a **horizontal scroll** section showing work experience as a timeline. The vertical scroll converts to horizontal motion via ScrollTrigger (`pin: true, scrub: true`).

```
[2024]──────[2025]──────[2026]──────[NOW]
            │           │           │
         Samsung      GSoC        LKMP
         PRISM     BeagleBoard.   Linux Kernel
                       org        Mentorship
```

The above is the rendered visual; actual data comes from the resume. The GSoC card explicitly references BeagleBoard.org (it is a real, public credential — unlike the SBC model, which is generic). The Samsung card respects `NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_SAMSUNG`. When Samsung is hidden, the timeline collapses to just GSoC and LKMP and the dashed connecting line redistributes.

Each entry is a vertical card with: company logo (monochrome treatment), role, dates, 2-line description, key tech tags. The timeline line itself is rendered with stroke-dashoffset animated by scroll (so it "draws" left-to-right as you scroll horizontally).

**Card hover effect:** the card's border picks up the same proximity-glow treatment as the hero grid cells.

## 8. Section 05 — TECH STACK (Constellation)

### 8.1 Concept: Constellation, Not Solar System

**Why not orbital solar system:** It's the default 3D dev portfolio cliché in 2025. Every bootcamp grad has one. It does not match the Vicharak aesthetic, which is restrained and architectural, not whimsical.

**Why constellation:** It reads as a knowledge graph — nodes (technologies) connected by faint lines (related technologies). It implies relationships ("FastAPI links to Python links to async") instead of arbitrary orbits. It also lets the layout be intentional rather than circularly symmetric.

### 8.2 Layout

Full viewport, slight 3D depth (subtle perspective, not aggressive). Nodes are small spheres or rounded icons (12–20px) labeled in mono caps below. Connecting lines are 1px, very low opacity (`rgba(255,255,255,0.12)`), with the connection only drawn between technologies that genuinely relate.

**Node groupings (clusters in space):**
- **Systems** (top-left): C, C++, Linux Kernel, Buildroot, Embedded C, ARM, I2C/SPI/UART, Device Tree
- **Backend** (top-right): Go, Python, FastAPI, async, WebSockets, REST, gRPC
- **AI/ML** (bottom-right): LangGraph, LangChain, ChromaDB, RAG, Embeddings, Qwen-VL, Tree-sitter
- **Infra** (bottom-left): Docker, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis
- **Bridges** between clusters: Python connects to both Backend and AI/ML. C connects to Systems and Embedded.

The clusters drift slowly (very slow — 60+ second cycle, barely perceptible). Mouse hover on a node:
- That node highlights to full opacity
- All directly connected nodes highlight to 50% opacity
- All connecting lines from the hovered node brighten to `rgba(255,255,255,0.5)`
- Other nodes fade to 30% opacity
- A small tooltip appears: technology name + one-line context ("used in GSoC kernel work" / "core of GitScope")

### 8.3 Alternative (if constellation proves too complex)

A **typographic stack list** — just gorgeous typography, three columns of tech names in mono caps, with hover triggering a subtle highlight and a context line below. No 3D needed. This is the safer, equally tasteful fallback. Vicharak-tier sites often choose typography over visualization.

**Recommendation:** Build the constellation. Keep the typographic list as fallback for mobile (constellation collapses to list under 768px width).

## 10. The Scroll Spline (Persistent Indicator)

Visible on every section except section 01 (where the scroll hint serves the role).

**Visual:**
- Fixed to the right edge of the viewport, ~24px from the edge
- Vertically centered, height ~50vh
- A single thin SVG path, 1px stroke, color `--border-active` at 30% opacity
- The path is **not straight** — it has a gentle, organic curve (think a slow S-curve)
- A small circle (the accent ice blue, 6px diameter) sits on the path at the position corresponding to scroll progress
- A faint glow around the circle (filter: drop-shadow blur 8px)

**Behavior:**
- As the user scrolls, the circle moves along the path
- The portion of the path *behind* the circle (already scrolled) is drawn at 60% opacity
- The portion *ahead* is drawn at 15% opacity
- Implemented with SVG + GSAP DrawSVG + MotionPath, scrubbed by scroll progress
- On hover, the circle expands slightly (6px → 9px) and tooltip shows current section name

**Critical detail:** the spline is not just a scroll bar. It is the **only colored element** on most of the site. It is the spine of the experience. Treat it with care.

---

## 11. The Custom Cursor

- Default cursor hidden site-wide
- A 6px dot, `--text-primary`, follows the mouse 1:1 (no lerp)
- A 36px ring, `--border-active`, follows with `lerp 0.12` (slight inertia)
- On hover over any interactive element, the ring scales to 60px and goes to `--accent`
- On press, the ring scales down to 24px
- Disabled on touch devices (use `@media (hover: hover)`)

---

## 12. Loading Sequence

The site needs a controlled load — the 3D model is heavy.

**Sequence:**
1. Page loads with the hero layout, but the name is hidden, grid is dim
2. A 1px line grows from 0% to 100% width along the bottom of the viewport while assets load
3. Once loaded, the line retracts to the center and disappears
4. Hero animation plays (name reveal, grid lights up)
5. Total time budget: ≤ 2.5 seconds on a fast connection, ≤ 5 seconds on 3G

Show the loader for a minimum of 800ms even on instant loads — sub-second loaders flash and feel broken.

---

## 13. Performance Budget

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| LCP | < 2.5s |
| FID / INP | < 100ms |
| CLS | < 0.05 (essentially zero — no layout shift allowed) |
| Total JS bundle | < 350KB gzipped (Three.js will dominate this) |
| .glb model | < 4MB |
| Lighthouse Performance | ≥ 85 on mobile |

**Optimizations required:**
- Three.js components dynamically imported (`next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`)
- GSAP plugins imported on-demand, not in root layout
- Fonts: `font-display: swap`, preload only the two weights actually used
- Images: Next.js Image component, AVIF + WebP
- Use `<Canvas frameloop="demand">` and `invalidate()` when state changes

---

## 14. Accessibility & Fallbacks

This is a heavy site. It must degrade gracefully.

**`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`:**
- Grid wall is static (no mouse reaction)
- SBC scene continues to render but rotation pauses; rim light snaps between features instead of interpolating
- Perimeter trace renders as a complete static outline (no progressive draw)
- Constellation does not drift
- Scroll spline simplifies to a vertical line with a dot
- Custom cursor disabled

**Keyboard navigation:**
- Tab order: skip nav → hero CTA → each project card → contact links
- All interactive elements have visible focus rings (`outline: 2px solid --accent; outline-offset: 4px`)
- Esc key resets cursor position / closes any expanded card

**Screen readers:**
- The 3D scene is `aria-hidden="true"` and decorative
- All project content is in real semantic HTML (h2/h3/p/ul), not baked into the canvas
- Each section has a proper `<section aria-labelledby="...">` structure

**No JS fallback:**
- Hero renders as plain text
- All project content is server-rendered and readable without any JS
- Static layout, no animations, but fully usable

---

## 15. Asset Manifest

What needs to exist before this can be built:

| Asset | Source | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Generic SBC .glb | Modeled in Blender (~1 hour, all primitives) | Stylized minimalist mockup. See §6.4 for full design spec. Named meshes required: `pcb`, `soc`, `mem_left`, `mem_right`, `pin_header`, `expansion_connector`, `io_left`, `io_right` |
| Small module .glb | Same modeling pass | A simple cube-with-pins, ~30mm square. Used briefly during the §6.3 project 5 (SIH/ESP32) lighting state as a faint companion module |
| Fonts | Fontshare (Cabinet Grotesk), Google Fonts (Inter), JetBrains | Self-host via `next/font` |
| Logos for companies | Samsung, Google Summer of Code, BeagleBoard, Linux Foundation, Thapar | All available as SVG; monochrome treatment in CSS |
| Project preview images | Vidhu's own screenshots | Used in case-study deep links (out of scope for v1) |
| HDRI for 3D scene | Pure black or subtle dark gradient | Custom .hdr or solid color |

## 16. Build Phases

Suggested phase order for Claude Code. Each phase must work end-to-end before moving on.

**Phase 1 — Skeleton (no animation):**
- Next.js setup, Tailwind, Lenis, GSAP wired up
- All six sections rendered as plain static layouts
- Colors, typography, spacing applied
- Mobile-responsive at breakpoints 768, 1024, 1440

**Phase 2 — Hero grid:**
- Canvas grid with mouse reactivity
- Hero text reveal
- Custom cursor

**Phase 3 — Scroll infrastructure:**
- Lenis + ScrollTrigger integration
- Scroll spline (without the 3D scene yet)
- Section pinning skeleton

**Phase 4 — 3D scene:**
- R3F canvas, lighting (key light + movable rim light), environment
- Generic SBC model loaded with all named meshes accessible
- Slow rotation behavior (with read-pause logic)
- Rim light interpolation between named meshes based on scroll progress
- Project cards in the right column synced to scroll
- Perimeter trace line drawing along PCB edge as scroll progresses

**Phase 5 — Polish:**
- Hero → SBC transition choreography (§5)
- Heat-shimmer particles on SoC during Samsung card
- Constellation section
- Loading sequence
- Reduced-motion fallbacks

**Phase 6 — Performance pass:**
- Lighthouse audit
- Bundle analysis
- Mobile testing on real devices

---

## 17. What This Site Must Not Do

A non-negotiable list. Any of these means the site has failed.

- Use a gradient background anywhere
- Use glassmorphism (frosted-glass cards with backdrop-blur)
- Have a Three.js scene that takes > 5 seconds to load on a fast connection
- Include any AI-generated stock 3D models or imagery
- Have more than three colors on screen at once (black, white, ice blue — that's it)
- Use Lottie animations
- Use a typewriter effect for body text (it's fine for the small label in §5)
- Have a "neon glow" anywhere
- Use any rounded button with a shadow that looks like every SaaS landing page
- Show a "scroll down" mouse icon with a bouncing wheel
- Have a "View my work ↓" with the bouncing arrow
- Use emojis as icons in the tech constellation
- Auto-play any audio
- Have a particle background drifting behind content (cliché since 2018)

---

## 18. The Final Test

Before shipping, take screenshots of every section at full resolution and at mobile width. Open them in sequence in a folder viewer.

If the sequence reads like a cohesive editorial design system — like the pages of a book by the same author — it ships.

If any frame looks like it was generated by a different person or a template, that frame must be reworked until it doesn't.

The brief was: *built by a designer with taste, not generated by an AI template.* That sentence is the acceptance criterion.

---

## 19. Modeling Note

The generic SBC model is the single biggest asset dependency. It is ~1 hour of Blender work using only primitive shapes (rounded cubes, beveled edges). No texturing pipeline needed beyond a subtle PCB trace pattern. The full geometry and material specification is in §6.1.1 — that section is detailed enough to hand directly to someone modeling the asset.

If modeling is outsourced, the deliverable is a single `.glb` file with named meshes (listed in §15). Do not accept a model with un-named or merged meshes — the camera targeting logic depends on querying meshes by name.

---

**End of spec.**
